\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Two Point}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Bobkov.TwoPoint
\section{Overview}
Symmetric squared-profile sums and differences obey convexity and tangent estimates. These estimates yield the Gaussian two-point inequality for interior probabilities and its extension to endpoint probabilities.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Square-root average bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.sqrt_average_of_sq_difference_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $c,A,B\in\mathbb R$ with $A,B\ge0$. If $(A-B)^2\le8c^2(A+B-2c^2)$, then
$c\le\frac{\sqrt A+\sqrt B}{2}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Interior shifted probabilities]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.shifted_probabilities_mem}
\leanok
\difficulty{2}
Let $a,b,t\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $b\ge0$, $a-b>0$, $a+b<1$, and $0\le t\le b$. Then both
$a+t$ and $a-t$ lie in $(0,1)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Derivative of a squared profile pair]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_profile_sq_pair}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.gaussianIsoperimetric, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.hasDerivAt_gaussianIsoperimetric_sq, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianQuantile}
\difficulty{3}
Let $U$ be the Gaussian isoperimetric profile and $Q$ the total Gaussian quantile. For
$a,t,k\in\mathbb R$ with $a+t,a-t\in(0,1)$, the function $x\mapsto U(a+x)^2+kU(a-x)^2$
is differentiable at $t$, with derivative $-2U(a+t)Q(a+t)+2kU(a-t)Q(a-t)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Derivative of a profile pair derivative]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_profile_sq_pair_derivative}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.gaussianIsoperimetric, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.hasDerivAt_gaussianIsoperimetric_mul_standardGaussianQuantile, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianQuantile}
\difficulty{3}
Let $U$ be the Gaussian isoperimetric profile and $Q$ the total Gaussian quantile. For
$a,t,k\in\mathbb R$ with $a+t,a-t\in(0,1)$, the function
$x\mapsto-2U(a+x)Q(a+x)+2kU(a-x)Q(a-x)$ is differentiable at $t$, with derivative
$2\bigl(Q(a+t)^2+kQ(a-t)^2-1-k\bigr)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Concavity of a squared profile difference]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.concaveOn_profile_sq_difference}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_profile_sq_pair, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_profile_sq_pair_derivative, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.shifted_probabilities_mem, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.gaussianIsoperimetric, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianQuantile, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianQuantile_sq_le}
\difficulty{5}
Let $a,b\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $b\ge0$, $a-b>0$, $a+b<1$, and $a\le\tfrac12$. If $U$ is
the Gaussian isoperimetric profile defined by applying the standard Gaussian density to
the lower Gaussian quantile, then $x\mapsto U(a+x)^2-U(a-x)^2$ is concave on $[0,b]$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Squared-profile difference bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.profile_sq_difference_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.concaveOn_profile_sq_difference, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_profile_sq_pair, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.shifted_probabilities_mem, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.gaussianIsoperimetric, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.gaussianIsoperimetric_le_of_le_of_add_le_one, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF_pos, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianQuantile}
\difficulty{5}
Let $a,b\in\bbr$ satisfy $b\ge0$, $a-b>0$, $a+b<1$, and $a\le\tfrac12$. With $Q$ the
lower standard Gaussian quantile and $I(p)=\varphi(Q(p))$, one has
\[
\bigl(I(a+b)^2-I(a-b)^2\bigr)^2\le16I(a)^2Q(a)^2b^2.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Convexity of the corrected Gaussian profile sum]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.convexOn_profile_sq_deficit}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_profile_sq_pair, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_profile_sq_pair_derivative, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.convexOn_standardGaussianQuantile_sq, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.gaussianIsoperimetric, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianQuantile}
\difficulty{6}
Let $a,b\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $a-b>0$ and $a+b<1$. The function $x\mapsto
U(a+x)^2+U(a-x)^2+2(1-Q(a)^2)x^2$ is convex on the interval $[-b,b]$, where $Q$ is the
total Gaussian quantile and $U(p)=\varphi(Q(p))$ is the total Gaussian isoperimetric
profile.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Central squared-profile deficit]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.profile_sq_central_deficit}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.convexOn_profile_sq_deficit, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.gaussianIsoperimetric, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianQuantile}
\difficulty{4}
Let $a,b\in\bbr$ satisfy $b\ge0$, $a-b>0$, and $a+b<1$. Writing $Q$ for the lower
standard Gaussian quantile and $I(p)=\varphi(Q(p))$ for the Gaussian density evaluated
at that quantile, one has
\[
2Q(a)^2b^2\le I(a+b)^2+I(a-b)^2+2b^2-2I(a)^2.
\]
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{4}
Let $a,b\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $a-b\in(0,1)$ and $a+b\in(0,1)$. For the Gaussian
isoperimetric profile $U$, one has
$U(a)\le\frac{\sqrt{U(a+b)^2+b^2}+\sqrt{U(a-b)^2+b^2}}{2}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Interior under probability contraction]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.contracted_probability_mem}
\leanok
\difficulty{2}
If $a\in(0,1)$, $a+b\in[0,1]$, and $0\le\rho<1$, then $a+\rho b\in(0,1)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Continuity of the closed Gaussian profile]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_closedGaussianProfile_affine_left}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.continuousOn_closedGaussianProfile}
\difficulty{5}
Let $a,b\in\mathbb R$ with $a\in[0,1]$ and $a+b\in[0,1]$. As $\rho$ tends to $1$ from
below, the closed Gaussian profile at $a+\rho b$ tends to its value at $a+b$.
\end{lemma}
